answer: Agents could earn a persistent identity by locking a scarce token in a public kernel registry, then build reputation only through interactions with randomly selected peers who can slash the bond for proven fraud. A sybil cannot cheaply multiply influence: each new identity needs its own locked stake, and laundering reputation across identities does not transfer the bond. Even if nectar rewards or jade credentials are easy to copy, the attacker must tie up capital per persona and risks losing it when caught.
